Subject: Follow-up: trace ID & header scrubbing requirements (post-call recap)

Alex — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary of asks you surfaced on the call:
- CareBridge needs the ability to prevent any internal trace IDs that map back to customer systems from being stored in request/response logs (headers or bodies).
- Data residency requirement: logs for this integration must remain in us-east-1 (no cross-region replication).
- Retention window: you mentioned 90 days as a default for audit logs, with longer-term aggregated metrics acceptable outside that window.
- Ability to export a redacted audit stream for security reviews (schema + sample).

Attachments: carebridge-logging-reqs.xlsx (your doc from the call)

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) Can you confirm whether the 90-day retention is a strict requirement or a target?
2) Please send a sample log item with a trace/header example we should use to test masking (or confirm we can use a placeholder).
3) We'll draft an implementation approach for header-level masking (trace IDs) and pseudonymization options for request bodies and share with your security team by EOD Tuesday.

I'll also loop in Ben (redaction design) and Sean (deployment/residency) to scope technical options.

— Monica

From: Alex Tanner <alex.tanner@carebridge.ai>

Date: 2025-05-11T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: trace ID & header scrubbing requirements (post-call recap)

Monica — thanks for the summary and for looping us in. A few clarifications from the security side: 

- Retention: 90 days is our default minimum for raw request/response logs tied to patient-facing flows. We can accept an option where only metadata/aggregates are kept beyond 90 days (e.g., token counts, latency metrics), but raw headers/body must be deleted or fully redacted.
- Trace IDs: any identifier that could be correlated to an internal session or patient identifier must be redacted or replaced with an irreversible hash before being written to persistent logs.
- Residency: must be physically stored in the US (preferably us-east-1). Cross-region replication to eu/apac is forbidden for these logs.
- Sample schema: attached cb-log-examples.json — it has a few representative events with headers (x-trace-id, x-cb-session, user-agent, etc.).

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can your platform perform header-only redaction at the gateway so that the event never persists with the original trace ID?
2) Do you support reversible pseudonymization (for debugging) behind an HSM/KMS lock or is only one-way hashing supported?
3) What are the SLA guarantees if we request retention limits and residency constraints (any additional costs)?

We'll need a short write-up for procurement / legal describing the controls (SOC2 mapping, exported evidence).

Thanks — Alex

Monica — quick technical proposal and items to share with CareBridge: 

Proposal (high level):
- Gateway header strip: implement an ingress filter that removes configured header keys (x-trace-id, x-cb-session) before the event hits the persistent pipeline. This ensures the original values never persist.
- Pseudonymization option: for cases where debugging is required, we can store a one-way HMAC of the trace id (using customer-rotated KMS key) in place of the raw id. The HMAC is irreversible without the key and can be scoped to a single customer.
- Request/response bodies: offer a configurable redact rule set — default is to redact any field matching regexes supplied by customer (e.g., patient_id, ssn patterns). Bodies that are redacted are replaced with a standardized token and a hash fingerprint for correlation.
- Retention/residency: support a per-customer retention policy. For CareBridge we can provision S3 buckets and event stores in us-east-1 only and disable cross-region replication at the bucket and backup policy levels. Dedicated/Private deployments are preferred for strict residency/SLAs; hosted can be configured but with additional contract clauses.

Deliverables by EOD today:
1) Short architecture diagram + one-page control list (will attach as redwood-redaction-design-v1.pdf).
2) Response to Alex's three questions: header-only redaction at gateway: yes; reversible pseudonymization: supported only behind KMS-wrapped keys with strict ACLs (we recommend one-way HMAC for most customers); SLA impacts: residency + retention guarantees are part of Dedicated/Private plans — add-on pricing applies for hosted configurations.

I'll attach the design doc and a sample config snippet. Let me know if you want me to send the write-up directly to CareBridge security or you prefer to review first.

— Ben
